reason: Skill reachability (#757 packaging fix, #756 dispatcher tier, #755 cassandra CLI): module-size 32960->33499 (+539). Attributed empirically, never arithmetically -- each unit was measured by moving one file aside (or restoring main's version of it) and re-running `harness check-arch --json` on the otherwise untouched branch. ts/src/core/skill-dispatch.ts is 144 of the 539 (33499 -> 33355 without it); ts/src/skills-cli.ts's edits are 112 (33499 -> 33387 with main's copy); ts/src/core/skill-registry.ts's edits are 65 (33499 -> 33434 with main's copy); ts/src/core/test-files.ts is 77 NET (33499 -> 33422 without it) even though the module is ~85 lines, because it is an EXTRACTION -- cli-commands.ts shed the same collector, so the only real cost is the new module's header and its exported doc comments. The residual ~141 is the two `skills run` sub-command registrations split out of buildSkillsCommand plus the doc blocks on the new exports; the split was made to retire a functionLength=56 finding this branch introduced, so it is a fix absorbed here rather than a violation absorbed here. Nothing outside ts/src contributes: moving BOTH of canary-cassandra's new scripts aside left the number at 33499 exactly, so module-size does not count the skill tree's .mjs at all, and the ts/test suites (skill-packaging, skill-dispatch, test-files, and the cassandra skill suite) are test code the metric also does not count. What the growth buys, in order of size. skill-dispatch.ts (144) is the tier-2 dispatcher #756 asked for: canary shipped tier 1 (spawn a declared cli:/entry: target) and tier 3 (a prose skill is unreachable) with nothing between, so 14 of 21 skills could not be invoked by any orchestrator, CI step, or sibling skill. Roughly half of that module is comment, deliberately, because four of its decisions are ones a later reader would otherwise reverse: dispatch resolves and returns the skill's contract rather than APPLYING the workflow (canary has no agent runtime, and pretending otherwise would have it claim answers it did not compute); every payload is stamped determinism='agent-applied' so a consumer merging findings across the four Tier-0 detectors can never mistake an agent's reading of a ruleset for a scanner's output, which is the confusion #755 documents; it is deliberately NOT gated by --allow-executable-skills, because that flag guards spawning a cloned overlay's code and dispatch spawns nothing -- gating it would leave the 14 skills unreachable in exactly the non-interactive contexts the issue is about; and an unreadable or body-less SKILL.md raises rather than returning empty, because a dispatcher that reported 'nothing to do' for a skill it could not read is indistinguishable from one that ran and found nothing. skills-cli.ts (112) is the dispatcher's rendering plus the #757 half: `No skills found.` was a confident claim about the world made by a check that had verified zero items, so an empty discovery now prints the abstention line and names all four search roots with whether each one existed. skill-registry.ts (65) is searchRoots(), which supplies that denominator, plus the exported bundledSkillsDirFrom() that lets ts/test/skill-packaging.test.ts pin the three-levels-up packaging contract that #757 turned out to hinge on. test-files.ts (77 net) exists so `canary vacuity-check` and the new canary-cassandra CLI ask the same question about which files are tests -- two collectors would have let the four detectors report different denominators for the same suite with neither number looking wrong. Splitting further would not help: module-size is a repo-wide aggregate, so N files summing to 539 score identically to one, and every new file is far under the per-file thresholds. Nothing was absorbed here to avoid a fix. The one NEW complexity violation this branch introduced (functionLength=56 in buildSkillsCommand) was FIXED by extracting registerRun/registerVerify, not allowed; newViolations is back to the single pre-existing parseDeclinedRows warning that main already carries (#767); and canary-cassandra's own cli.mjs main() was split into scan/report for the same reason even though the skill tree is outside this metric entirely. No baseline was refreshed and no threshold was raised.
